title: PreCompact Hook Blocking + Background Plugin Monitors (v2.1.105)
description: Two related v2.1.105 hook system expansions. (1) PreCompact Hook Blocking: hooks can now block compaction entirely by exiting with code 2 OR returning JSON `{"decision":"block"}`. Previously, PreCompact hooks could inspect/modify compaction state but not veto it. This enables quality gates: block compaction if critical state would be lost, if active subagents are running, or if mid-task context must be preserved. (2) Background Plugin Monitors: a new top-level `monitors` key in the plugin manifest that auto-arms background monitor scripts at session start or on skill invoke. Enables persistent background monitoring (test watchers, file change detectors, cost monitors) without manual hook setup. Related: /proactive is now an alias for /loop (autonomous task mode). Released April 2026.
redundancy_check: IMPROVEMENT over existing PreCompact hook (already in registry). PreCompact hook existed but was observational only. Exit code 2 blocking is a meaningful capability expansion — matches PreToolUse/PermissionRequest blocking semantics, brings PreCompact to full parity. Background monitors manifest is NOVEL — no existing mechanism for auto-armed persistent background processes in plugins.
notes: PreCompact blocking is directly useful for the iterative-improve pipeline: block compaction when loop state is active. Background monitors could replace manual hook setup for clauditor-style session monitoring patterns. The `monitors` manifest key is new infrastructure for plugin ecosystem — worth documenting in hook-lifecycle skill as the 22nd+ hook mechanism. Verify exact manifest schema from Anthropic docs before integrating.

evaluation.reasoning: Integration complexity (80): moderate — update existing PreCompact hook scripts to use exit code 2 for veto logic; background monitors requires new manifest key but is straightforward config. Token efficiency (60): blocking compaction when critical iterative-improve state is active prevents expensive context reconstruction; minor but real saving. Capability expansion (75): PreCompact blocking upgrades an observational hook to a gating hook (aligns with PreToolUse/PermissionRequest blocking semantics, brings parity); background monitors is genuinely novel infrastructure with no existing equivalent. Maintenance burden (80): hook scripts are static once configured; monitors manifest is stable. Community validation (80): official Anthropic v2.1.105 release. Integration type: TECHNIQUE — update hook-lifecycle skill to add blocking decision return, add monitors manifest documentation, and document /proactive alias.
